newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-IN-FORM COLE SINKS HIS OLD CLUB ARSENAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-IN-FORM COLE SINKS HIS OLD CLUB ARSENAL.

text.p: Striker Andy Cole reaffirmed his return to form by scoring one goal and creating another as Manchester United beat his former club Arsenal 2-1 to stay top of the English premier league on Wednesday night.

Cole, rejected by the Gunners as a youngster after just one appearance, put the champions ahead after 18 minutes in his first full league game of a frustrating season which has seen him stuck on the substitutes' bench and sidelined with a cracked shin bone.
He set up Norway's Ole Gunnar Solskjaer for United's second 14 minutes later and although Dutch striker Dennis Bergkamp scored for Arsenal after the break the Londoners could not find an equaliser.

"I've been trying to get over all my setbacks and I'm just enjoying my football. It's always nice to come back to Highbury," said Cole, who has struggled since joining United for a club record 6.25 million pounds ($10 million) from Newcastle in 1995.
Both United's goals came from counter-attacks.
For the first, Cole latched onto a long ball out of defence from Gary Neville and waltzed past Arsenal goalkeeper John Lukic before guiding the ball into an empty net.
The second goal came as United broke with devastating speed from their own penalty area following an Arsenal corner.

Ryan Giggs sped down the left wing and flicked the ball inside to Karel Poborsky who in turn found Cole. He laid off a perfectly weighted pass to Solskjaer who drilled a left foot shot past Lukic into the bottom corner of the net.
Arsenal marksman Ian Wright was lucky not to be sent off after a reckless two-footed challenge on Peter Schmeichel which left the United goalkeeper writhing in agony on the edge of his penalty area.

Wright, who had been booked before the incident, claimed the Dane was play-acting and as the players left the pitch after the final whistle he had to be restrained by stewards as he tried to confront Schmeichel.
Police then intervened to keep the two players apart.
United manager Alex Ferguson leapt off the bench at the time of the challenge but refused to comment on it afterwards. "I've got a view but I'd rather keep it to myself," he said.
The two players were involved in an ugly incident in the league match at Old Trafford in November when Schmeichel was caught on television cameras mouthing a racist insult at Wright, who is black.
United's victory kept them a point clear of Liverpool who spoilt Ian Rush's return to Anfield by beating Leeds 4-0.

Rush, who scored 229 league goals for Liverpool before joining Leeds on a free transfer in the close season, started as a substitute but came on with 17 minutes remaining to a thunderous reception from an ever-generous Anfield crowd.

By then though Leeds were doomed. Robbie Fowler put Liverpool ahead with a typical close range effort after 21 minutes and striking partner Stan Collymore scored twice in two minutes to wrap up the points before halftime.
England midfielder Jamie Redknapp scored Liverpool's fourth goal three minutes from the final whistle.

United and Liverpool have now opened up a gap at the top of the table for the first time this season. United have 53 points from 26 games to Liverpool's 52. Third-placed Arsenal have 48 points and have played one game more.

Trinidadian striker Dwight Yorke struck twice as Aston Villa won 2-1 to ensure Midlands neighbours Coventry went away from Villa Park empty handed yet again. Coventry have never won at Villa Park in 23 league matches dating back to 1937.
Derby and Sheffield Wednesday shared in a 2-2 draw while Newcastle's clash at West Ham was postponed due to a waterlogged pitch.
